summary: This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to remove parents from immediate-relative status, eliminate all family preference categories except spouses and children of permanent residents, cap such visas at 88,000 per year, and create a new temporary nonimmigrant W visa for parents of adult U.S. citizens that bars work authorization and public benefits.

scores.thoughts: The bill makes no changes to federal spending levels, appropriations, or budget authority. It only restructures certain immigration categories and creates a new nonimmigrant classification with eligibility restrictions.
The bill contains no tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures.

The bill requires that parents admitted under the new nonimmigrant (W) classification must have private health insurance arranged by their U.S.-citizen child at no cost to the parent. This is a narrow eligibility condition rather than any systemic change to healthcare policy or coverage models.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly and substantially amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to eliminate parents as immediate relatives, eliminate most family preference categories, cap family-sponsored immigration at 88,000 visas per year, and replace permanent immigration options for parents with a strictly limited 5-year nonimmigrant status that prohibits work and public benefits. These changes are explicitly intended to reduce family-based immigration numbers and pathways.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affect military or defense spending or policy.
No provisions address environmental regulation, climate policy, or natural resources.

The bill bars new nonimmigrant (W) parents from any federal, state, or local public benefits and places financial responsibility on their U.S.-citizen children. This is a narrow restriction tied to a new visa category rather than a general change to welfare programs.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No provisions address deficits, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting rights, election administration, or voter eligibility.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions address labor law, union rights, or employment standards.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
